evidence.text: Topics. algorithms and auction dynamics / Deconstructing Meta's Andromeda algorithm and the shift to vector-based targeting, where the ad creative itself dictates audience selection, replacing deprecated interest/lookalike targeting. Explaining the "Creative Similarity Score" and how Andromeda bundles visually or thematically similar creatives under a single entity ID; this restricts unique reach, forces ads to compete for the same cluster, and artificially drives up frequency while degrading Return on Ad Spend (ROAS). Managing ad sequencing within the algorithm, recognizing that Meta optimizes for multi-click and view-through journeys, making ad-level last-click ROAS highly unreliable for top-of-funnel creative. campaign setup and tracking / Architecting ad accounts to support algorithmic learning by consolidating creative variations into concept-specific adsets (Persona + Angle + Offer). Avoiding the common error of segmenting adsets by arbitrary traits (e.g., launch dates) or mixing conflicting personas (e.g., men and women) within the same adset, which confuses the machine learning targeting models. Managing the risk of Dynamic Product Ads (DPAs) causing a "death spiral" by masking poor top-of-funnel performance with inflated bottom-of-funnel retargeting ROAS. scaling / Implementing a portfolio management approach to ad scaling to avoid the risk of relying on a single "hero ad" that inevitably reaches its maximum daily spend capacity and fatigues. Utilizing Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) to leverage Pareto’s Principle (where 4% of ads command 64% of spend) for maximum efficiency, while carefully monitoring to prevent over-concentration that exposes the business to sudden revenue drops. Recommending a minimum allocation of 10% to 25% of the total media budget directly toward creative production to maintain the volume required to combat ad fatigue.
